title: Rational supported finite models are finite extensions of localized integral models
statement: Fix a prime ell and commutative condensed rings R,K identified by ring-object isomorphisms with either (Z_ell,Q_ell) or (O_E,E) for one finite intermediate extension E/Q_ell, all with the full continuous-map condensed rings [sk-def-localizing-closure]. On a qcqs scheme T use ordinary uncompleted module-derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-size-convention]. There exists a ring-object map a:R -> K satisfying IsEllLocalizationCoefficient [lem-sfb-supported-coefficient-localization]. Define IsLocalizedSupportedModel(a,T) to consist of all derived objects isomorphic to (K_T tensor_R_T J_R H)[0], where J_R is extension along any path in any finite qcqs open-closed tree rooted at T [def-sfb-qcqs-open-closed-tree] and H is a finite scalar local model on that path source [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Then for every such path with source S and every finite scalar K_S-local model L, there is n in N such that (J_K L)[0] belongs to extensionProductIter n of IsLocalizedSupportedModel(a,T): n=0 is the generators, and a successor permits a distinguished triangle whose first object is a generator and whose third is in the preceding class. All maps are actual K-linear maps. There is no closed pair or comparison hypothesis, and no assumption of a global lattice for L.

proof.text: Transport the standard inclusion Z_ell -> Q_ell or O_E -> E through the specified two ring-object isomorphisms; for Q_ell use the bottom finite intermediate field. The coefficient-localization theorem gives exact scalar extension and the regular ell-telescope at every scheme, including its specified zeroth leg.

Every source of a path is qcqs. A finite scalar local model over the field has finite-dimensional local presentations; choose finite bases and use the constant finite-free comparison to make it lisse, hence constructible on the single stratum. Varying ranks and rank zero are permitted.

Apply the qcqs stratified integral-lattice theorem and refine the root tree by the resulting finite constructible lattice partition. Its nonempty leaves have lisse integral lattices spanning the rational restrictions. Empty leaves carry zero. Append each branch to the original path, adjoining complementary siblings. The resulting paths are still admissible.

The lattice-tree scalar comparison identifies each supported leaf with scalar extension of its integral supported branch. Along the original path apply the open slice projection and closed underived projection formulas. Internal-sectionwise transport and Cartesian coefficient compatibility ensure these are comparisons for the actual internal functors.

All edge functors are exact. Each open-closed short exact sequence gives a distinguished triangle after passage to degree-zero complexes and extension along the original path. The finite-tree reconstruction theorem, or induction with extensionProductIter_add, expresses the root object as a finite iterated extension of the supported rational leaves. Repleteness of IsLocalizedSupportedModel replaces these leaves by their scalar-extension presentations. Arbitrary actual connecting maps are retained; the root path and zero leaves require no special assumptions.
